memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: God made two great lights—the greater light to govern the day and the lesser light to govern the night. He also made the stars. - Gen 1:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God makes two great lights, the sun to rule the day and the moon to rule the night, and almost in passing, the verse adds, "He also made the stars." Those countless stars that fill us with wonder are mentioned here as though they were a small addition. What is vast and breathtaking to us is a simple word from God's mouth. This is the greatness of our Maker.

Notice something the writer of Genesis is quietly doing. In the surrounding cultures of that time, people worshipped the sun, moon, and stars as gods. But here they are shown to be nothing more than created things, made by the one true God to serve His purposes. The sun is not a god; it is a lamp God hung in the sky. Creation is never meant to be worshipped, only the Creator is.

This guards our hearts today. It is easy to give the highest place in our lives to created things, money, success, people, comfort. But all of these are only gifts, made by God. He alone deserves our worship.

The sun and moon "govern" day and night, yet they answer to God. One day a greater light will make even the sun unnecessary, for the Lord Himself will be our light (Rev 21:23). Let your wonder at the skies lead you to worship the God who made them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there any created thing you have been giving the place in your heart that belongs to God alone?
2. How can the beauty of the sun, moon, and stars lead you to worship the Creator?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You made the sun, moon, and stars with a single word. Keep my heart from worshipping created things, and help me give my worship to You alone. Amen.
